Message to U.S. Citizens: 
Demonstration Alert: Large-Scale Anti-Corruption Protests
https://t.co/ji7nPMuWf5

Location: EDSA People Power Monument in Quezon City and Rizal (Luneta) Park in Manila.

Event: Large-Scale Anti-Corruption Protests Scheduled in Metro Manila – November 30

Two rallies are scheduled for Sunday, November 30, 2025. The first will take place at the EDSA People Power Monument in Quezon City with approximately 100,000 expected attendees. The second rally will occur at Luneta Park, situated 500 meters from the Embassy Compound and four kilometers from the Seafront Compound. Police estimate 5,000 will attend.

In addition to these two main events, simultaneous demonstrations are planned across 29 locations throughout Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. The Embassy encourages U.S. citizens to follow local news for information about possible protest activity in your area.

Actions to Take:  

•U.S. citizens should avoid the rallies, as even peaceful rallies/demonstrations have the potential to turn violent without warning. Foreign nationals found engaging in a protest or mass demonstration could be considered in violation of their immigration status.

•Follow local media and government sources for updates on possible disruptions and re-routing schemes as heavy traffic congestion and road closures are expected near protest venues.

•Follow instructions from local authorities.

•Exercise caution when in the vicinity of any large gatherings.

For further information and assistance:

•Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (https://t.co/q8w0nZfWZo) to receive Alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.

•Contact the U.S. Embassy in Manila, Philippines, located at 1201 Roxas Boulevard, at +(63) (2) 5301-2000, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. After-hours emergency number for U.S. citizens is +(63) (2) 5301-2000.

•Call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free in the United States and Canada or 1-202-501-4444 from other countries from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time, Monday through Friday (except U.S. federal holidays).

•See the State Department’s travel website(https://t.co/Tiyt8sq7F9) for the Worldwide Caution, Travel Advisories, Alerts, and the Philippines Country Specific Information (https://t.co/ApMa3LxNZy).

Residents in the flood-prone province of Bulacan on Thursday (November 27) expressed outrage over alleged corruption that left communities submerged and businesses shuttered.

Despite billions of pesos allocated for flood mitigation, officials remain unpunished fuelling public anger.

“The flood here is severe. Every day it is flooded. Students, regular citizens, businessmen, all kinds of people are affected. Many businesses have already closed. Classes are often online, and it’s not effective for small children. When the rain is strong and the tide is high, classes are suspended. The kids don’t learn properly, what will happen to the next generation of Hagonoy?” said 54-year-old Hagonoy resident, Matilde Sanchez.

Residents said their frustration goes beyond inconvenience, describing the corruption as systemic and inhumane. Many feel they have been robbed not only of funds meant to protect them, but of normal ways of living.

"We don't feel anything but anger. Anger towards the heartless who greedily corrupted money that was meant to solve these kinds of calamities," Sanchez added.

The Philippines has long struggled with flood control scandals. Billions of pesos intended for flood mitigation projects were allegedly siphoned off through ghost projects that were never completed, leaving towns like Hagonoy submerged whenever tides rise and heavy rains hit.

Public anger has grown as government agencies has yet to prosecute those responsible. Critics say corruption in the Philippines has spread across branches and agencies, affecting countless communities and eroding trust in public institutions.

As demonstrators prepare for a protest in Manila on November 30, residents of Hagonoy said they will bring the voices of flood-stricken communities to the nation’s capital, demanding accountability and immediate action to prevent further disasters.

COURTESY: Reuters
